questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Speed of an Object
questions.problem: A glacier moves $49$ feet in $14$ months, moving at a constant rate. What is the speed of the glacier?
questions.worked_solution:
Speed is a special unit rate applied to moving objects. It is defined as *the distance traveled per unit of time*:

$$
\text{speed}=\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}
$$

To find the speed, in feet per month, we divide the number of feet $49,$ by the number of months, $14.$ This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{49}{14} & =\frac{49÷7}{14÷7} \\  & =\frac{7}{2} \\  & =7÷2 \\  & =3.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the speed of the glacier is $3.5$ feet per month.

questions.problem: It takes $3$ seconds for a peregrine falcon to fly $51$ meters when moving at a constant pace. Find the distance the peregrine falcon covers in $7$ seconds.
questions.worked_solution:
Speed is a special unit rate applied to moving objects. It is defined as *the distance traveled per unit of time*:

$$
\text{speed}=\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}
$$

To find the speed in meters per second, we divide the number of meters $51,$ by the number of seconds, $3.$ This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{51}{3} & =51÷3 \\  & =17.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the speed of the peregrine is $17$ meters per second. 

To find the distance covered in $7$ minutes, we multiply the speed by $7.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{distance} & =\text{speed}\times \text{time} \\  & =17\times 7 \\  & =119.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the peregrine falcon covers $119$ meters in $7$ seconds.

canonical_examples.problem: It takes $5$ days for the Earth to travel $13$ million kilometers around the Sun. How much time does it take for the Earth to travel $52$ million kilometers around the Sun?
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Speed is a special unit rate applied to moving objects. It is defined as *the distance traveled per unit of time*:

$$
\text{speed} = \dfrac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}
$$

To find the speed, in millions of kilometers per day, we divide the number of million kilometers, $13,$ by the number of days, $5.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{13}{5} & =13÷5 \\  & =2.6.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the speed of the Earth is $2.6$ million kilometers per day. 

To find the time it takes the Earth to cover $52$ million kilometers, we divide the distance by $2.6.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{time} & =\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}} \\  & =\frac{52}{2.6} \\  & =\frac{52\times 10}{2.6\times 10} \\  & =\frac{520}{26} \\  & =520÷26 \\  & =20.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, it takes the Earth $20$ days to travel $52$ million kilometers around the Sun.
